data.name: The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind® Game of the Year Edition
data.detailed_description:
The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind® Game of the Year Edition includes Morrowind plus all of the content from the Bloodmoon and Tribunal expansions. The original Mod Construction Set is not included in this package.
An epic, open-ended single-player RPG, Morrowind allows you to create and play any kind of character imaginable. You can choose to follow the main storyline and find the source of the evil blight that plagues the land, or set off on your own to explore strange locations and develop your character based on their actions throughout the game. Featuring stunning 3D graphics, open-ended gameplay, and an incredible level of detail and interactivity, Morrowind offers a gameplay experience like no other.
In Tribunal, you journey to the capital city of Morrowind, called Mournhold, to meet the other two god-kings of Morrowind, Almalexia and Sotha Sil. Your journey will lead you to the Clockwork City of Sotha Sil and massive, epic-sized dungeons, where strange and deadly creatures await you, including goblins, lich lords, and the mysterious Fabricants.
Bloodmoon takes you to the frozen Island of Solstheim where you'll experience snow, blizzards, and new creatures, including frost trolls, ice minions, and wolves... just to name a few. You'll have a choice of stories to follow and have the opportunity to defend the colony, take control over how the colony is built up, and eliminate the werewolves. Or, you can decide to join the werewolves and become one of them, opening up a whole new style of gameplay.
Key features:
  • Players can take their existing Morrowind characters and save games and continue their adventures in the Morrowind GotY edition
  • Adds up to 80 hours of new gameplay and quests for current Morrowind players
  • Explore the forests, caves, and snow-covered wastelands of the island of Solstheim
  • Delve into new, epic-sized dungeons and visit the Capital City of Mournhold and the Clockwork City of Sotha Sil
  • Fight new creatures including bears and wolves, lich lords and goblins, ice minions and spriggans
  • Direct the construction of a mining colony and face the threat of savage werewolves
  • Become a werewolf and indulge your thirst for the hunt
  • New armor and weapons including Nordic Mail and Ice blades

reviews.review:
Have you ever loved someone? Really loved someone? Have you ever shed the existential fear of being alone inside your own mind forever? Do you know what comes after death? Will anyone come to mourn you when you pass, and are you simply drifting in a world that doesn't care whether or not you make anything of your life? Do you jack off too much? 

Well none of that bull shit matters 'cause we have Morrowind and it's the best game to come out in Current Year 2002. Have a fishystick, dumbass, your one portal to feeling normal has finally opened and maybe, just maybe, you'll make [i]one[/i] friend on the forum. You're 25, working a dead-end job and everyone is blaming you for not being in an Ivy League college already. Maybe you blame yourself, too. You can remember the last time you felt happy. It was playing Dungeons and Dragons in high school when you still had friends, before you moved to Chicago. Getting to exist in a world that has [i]reason[/i] and [i]meaning[/i] where everyone is willing to talk to you no matter how Undiagnosed Autistic you are really made you feel alive. You pretended, for a good long while, that it made you better at social interaction; It obviously didn't or you'd have had gotten another girlfriend after Lindsey broke up with your sorry ass two years ago. Still hurts, doesn't it? Oh, Boo Hoo, Maybe she'll message you on AIM again. But, please... don't get your hopes up. That's even more sad. Morrowind isn't DnD. It's not even like playing DnD. But it's as close as DnD can feel behind a screen. Except, of course, all of those DnD games Interplay made, but you never really liked Fallout or Planescape or Baldur's Gate, no; Too communistic for your fragile pragmatically-conservative-but-ideally-progressive still-in-denial-about-being-a-lesbian-but-you've-only-dated-women attitude toward political art. Lindsey would love Morrowind. Christ, you're hopeless. 

Why do you like Morrowind? 'Cause Morrowind makes you feel good. You come home after a long shift and you turn on the PC you could barely afford and know will just be outdated in a few short years to play this stupid new BethesdaSoft game with it's stupid Dark Elves and stupid House Dagoth and stupid Empire and stupid Dwarves and stupid Daedra and maybe feel like you belong somewhere for a while. Josh from work showed you that you can drag and drop mp3 files into the music folder and they'll just work. You set the combat tracks to Limp Bizkit and NIN and the calm tracks to Sublime and Pink Floyd. You could get lost in this deep world for hours, and you have. You never needed Lindsey. You never wanted to marry her. Shit... It's so hard, now, to get immersed in something. Despite how screwed up your parents are, you regret not experiencing more things as a child. You regret becoming an adult. But that's not how entropy works, dig? And guess what? You [i]did[/i] love someone. Really love someone. And now she's gone, 'cause you're a fuck-up. You should've listened to her more, you should've given her more space, you should've asked for less and been more and did more and be perfect and should've given every ounce of your essence to satiate the drop-dead-gorgeous Goddess of Cancer. 3 years! God! 3 years you dated her. You should've gone to college and been in forever debt, obviously. Maybe that would've saved you the months you spent terrified to sleep in fear that you die without having done anything with your life... You stare at the pause screen a lot. Maybe you should get that checked out. 

You don't really notice time pass anymore. It feels like every email you send says "Sent 14 days ago" within only a couple hours. You worry you might have cancer. You worry about every passing car and every open-carrying cowboy type. You worry about your future, your career, your diet, and your empty queen bed. You got into Feng Shui in '99 but no matter how many times you re-arrange your furniture, you can't seem to push your life forward into the direction that it ought to be in. Maybe Dad is right. Maybe you really do drive the failure in your own life. Maybe it really is [i]your fault[/i] she left. There you go again, thinking about her. [i]Maybe[/i] if you got off your lazy ass and actually go to bars and flirt with people you'd- oh, right, yeah, you suck at eating pussy. You wear your Doc Martens and Surplus Pants as if signaling to other women that you're gay-or-something means you'll get some. Please. Like you're so special. Like you have what it takes to be better than her, because that's what it has always been about. Being superior to those you think wronged you. Do you really think she deserves to be with you? After what you've done? Everything you've ever done is a race for pity, all the way to the fucking bottom. And that is exactly where [i]you[/i] are.

The bottom, [i]The Abyss[/i], your lowest, James Cameron. Everest doesn't stand as tall as Challenger is deep, and not a single ray of light penetrates so far. You'll never summit Everest. Don't think of it as the goal, but as a treat if you ever make it there. Surfacing is your goal. You focus on the negative, ruminate obsessively, and you wonder why you can't sleep at night. You're stonger than you'd think, though. You're still going, aye? You bend like a singing saw, and you've yet to break. You can still appreciate the little things, sometimes, like long walks and High Fantasy videogames and a hot cocoa on christmas and a cool pillow and the embrace of a lover... even if she's gone and not coming back. You trudge the trenches of mediocrity toward the warm light that penetrates thick clouds. You feed the ducks at the park. You let others pass before yourself. You look at the stars, imagine the heavens above, and you can see that you exist at the center of yourself, cast out from Oblivion like a dremora who fell to Nirn. You're beautiful. You're hopeless. You're amazing. There's nobody [i]I'd[/i] rather spend eternity with. I love you. Wholly and truly. You make me wake up in the morning. You give me reason to breathe and walk through this stupid world we find ourselves in. You're the only you I have. I love you, stupid, I love you. 

I criticize you because I love you. I want to see you happy, but you can't even start when you're still feeling sorry for yourself. I hope that, even if you don't understand now, that one day you will. And one day you'll play Oblivion, and Skyrim, and whatever comes next. And I wake up every damn day expecting my own life to change. That's why I love Morrowind. In Morrowind, I can change.

[i]And I miss you, dreadfully.[/i]
